families.name: Kanyō
families.description: Kanyō is a computer-vision system that has watched Harvard's falcon cameras around the clock since early 2026, and the Viewer is the public website where anyone can browse what it saw. Kanyō does the watching — detecting birds, recording arrivals and departures, sending alerts — and the Viewer turns those recordings into a site you can visit. It was built by a designer with no engineering background and runs in production for a real researcher.

families.name: Edelmore
families.description: Edelmore is a pair of reading-and-writing tools built for my own children, sharing one codebase and one idea: software can feel like a real book. The Diary opens to today's page, takes dictation, and reads entries back aloud. The Reader turns an ebook into a read-along book, each word glowing as it is spoken. They were built for specific kids the mainstream options were failing — a tool made for one person, done fully, is a complete project.

families.name: Kṣetra-Ops
families.description: Kṣetra-Ops is a set of tools for people who run their own servers and want to actually understand them. Most options force a choice: hand control to someone else's cloud, or earn it the hard way at the command line. These tools refuse the choice — they are friendly interfaces that keep the command line's full power and transparency underneath. It is power over your own machines, held in the open.

families.name: Shōjiki (正直)
families.description: Shōjiki is the hands-on-the-machines toolkit. Pālana is the workbench for managing files and services across your servers; Forteller pushes configuration out from one source of truth; Sharibako keeps API keys and secrets encrypted on your own disk; and sageframe-mcp lets AI agents read the same live picture of the machines. The name is 正直, honesty, because every tool shows you exactly what it is doing.

families.name: Nen (念)
families.description: Nen holds the backup discipline. Hōzō copies data snapshots to a backup machine that wakes only when needed and sleeps the rest of the time, and Sage ZFS checks the whole backup picture — what is protected, what is stale, what would actually restore. The name is 念, mindfulness, because a backup is a promise you have to keep checking.

families.name: The Ho Range
families.description: Everything on this map was built with the methodology that lives here. The Ho System is a discipline for building real software with AI while keeping your own judgment: the human makes the architectural decisions, the AI implements, and every session is bounded and reviewed. Dandori extends the discipline to autonomous agents, and Kinhin is the workbench where a practitioner watches their own practice develop. You can ship serious software with AI without becoming someone who cannot ship alone — the rest of this map is the evidence.

families.name: The Actually Range
families.description: This range is a new way to teach technical subjects, built on curiosity and exploration. *, Actually is the engine: it turns a folder of layered explanations into a website where you arrive with a question and read only as deep as you need. SSH, Actually and Ho, Actually are the first instances — one teaches SSH, a tool every developer uses and few were ever taught well; the other teaches the methodology this whole body of work runs on.

families.name: Sageframe
families.description: Sageframe is the start of it all — the organizing system the whole body of work grew out of. The vault is where the thinking lives; Keisaku reads the current state of every project straight from the work itself, so the record is never stale; and Shoshin no Sono — the map you are looking at — draws it all as one territory.

families.name: Kekkai (結界)
families.description: The Kekkai range gathers the instruments for a hard question: when you work with AI for months, how do you keep the work — and the voice — yours? Sutra is a writing tool with the power of version control and none of its interface, and Shodō makes years of AI conversations searchable. Around the Interference site gather the four instruments that catch the drift: Voice DNA mirrors your voice back to you, Superposition helps a non-writer produce something genuinely theirs, Kiku scans a conversation history for known failure patterns, and Destructive Interference names the eight ways AI-shaped prose goes wrong. The name is 結界, the ritual boundary.

families.name: Constructive Interference
families.description: Constructive Interference is the writing practice of the body of work — essays on Substack about the methodology, the tools, and what months of collaboration with a machine actually feel like. An essay about a specific project settles on the map beside that project; the rest gather here, a city at the mountain's base.

shoshin-no-sono.name: Shoshin no Sono
shoshin-no-sono.hero: The map that argues the works are one project.

interference.hero: Voice and machine, held in phase.

new_works.name: Ho, Actually
new_works.hero: The methodology, taught under its own discipline.
new_works.short_description: The Ho System taught as a navigable graph — a depth-layered guide to the methodology, built on the *, Actually engine. Enter with a question, dial the depth, stop when you understand enough.
substantive_description: The second live instance of *, Actually, and the reflexive one: the methodology documented under its own discipline. Where SSH, Actually proves the engine generalizes outward to an external domain, Ho, Actually turns it inward — the Ho System's concepts, stages, and document chain organized by question and relationship rather than by chapter order, each node readable at the depth the reader needs.

relationships.note: A content repo supplying nodes and a site.yaml to the shared engine.

new_works.name: Constructive Interference
new_works.hero: The writing is the argument the work makes about itself, in public.
new_works.short_description: The essay practice of the body of work — Constructive Interference at sageframe.substack.com, where the collaboration writes about itself: methodology, voice, agency, and what months of working with a machine actually do to a practitioner. The mountain the collected writings settle beneath.
substantive_description: Human voice and machine assistance can either cancel or reinforce, depending on whether they are held in phase — the wave metaphor the whole body of work draws its name from. The Substack is where that thesis is worked out in public, essay by essay: not documentation of the tools but the argument they exist inside. Project essays settle as towns near the works they document; the rest gather here, a city at the mountain's base.

new_works.name: Sageframe on Medium
new_works.short_description: The second outlet — selected essays republished for a broader audience at medium.com/@sageframe. A lower shoulder on the Constructive Interference mountain.
